Downloaded PDF and extracted text: Amtsblatt Nr. 14 a, Sonderamtsblatt, 31 March 2025; ordinance signed Augsburg 28.03.2025 (OB Eva Weber); two rates 2.60 and 1.00 euro/h; Parkzone 1 covers resident areas A, B, C fully and D, F within the listed boundary (Viktoriastrasse ... Oberer Graben ... Halderstrasse); para 3 Grossveranstaltungen fee 0.50-10.00 euro per car. Supports text as written.

City page title 'Parkgebühren & Bezahlmöglichkeiten | Parken in Augsburg'. Page says since 01.04.2025 electric cars (vehicles with E-Kennzeichen) park free up to 3 hours in Augsburg and all Bavaria; parking disc required; posted maximum duration still applies.

Page confirms resident parking since November 2023, Bauausschuss resolution of 11.03.2022, 80 percent as the threshold for high parking pressure (high pressure found in both Nord and Sued), 1 euro/h, 30 euro one-year permit. But the current zone list gives 3 hours maximum for paid zones, with '9:30-18:30' weekdays; the 'blue zones' label appears only in an older passage tied to a 2-hour limit, so '(blue zones)' and the blanket '3 hours' are shaky. Also the page says the city 'cites' the 80 percent only as the definition of high pressure.
items.corrected_text: Resident-parking management has applied in the Rosenau and Thelott districts since November 2023, following a Bauausschuss resolution of 11 March 2022; the city says 80 percent occupancy marks high parking pressure and that high pressure was found in both the northern and southern areas. Paid parking applies on weekdays 9:30-18:30 at the current fee of 1 euro per hour with a maximum stay of three hours (resident-permit holders are exempt in the relevant zones), and a resident permit costs 30 euro for one year.

items.note: City news page (16.12.2022) is an announcement of a planned trial: 1 May 2023 to 30 April 2024, northern Maximilianstrasse plus Apothekergaesschen, Winter- and Dominikanergasse; 50 spaces in Maximilianstrasse and 9 in Winter-/Dominikanergasse to be dissolved ('werden aufgeloest'). Draft writes it as having run/removed; the page only supports plan wording. The Aug 2023 court order (item 5) shows the pedestrian zone had to be undone.
items.corrected_text: In December 2022 the city announced a traffic trial from 1 May 2023 to 30 April 2024 that would turn northern Maximilianstraße (between Herkules and Merkurbrunnen) plus Apothekergässchen, Winter- and Dominikanergasse into a pedestrian zone, with 50 parking spaces in Maximilianstraße and 9 in Winter-/Dominikanergasse to be removed.

items.note: DAZ 16 July 2025, title matches. The report describes a proposal: the Stellplatzsatzung decision was 'diesen Donnerstag' on the Bauausschuss agenda; city 'soll' reduce required spaces to 80 percent of the cap in Kern- and Kernrandzone (up to 50 percent possible for climate adaptation), max 2 spaces per flat in free housing, no obligation for single-/two-family and row houses from 1 Oct 2025, and Ablöse core zone 13,500 -> 18,000 euro. The draft does not say these are proposed and outcome is unknown. Medium confidence; weak, partly outdated item.
items.corrected_text: A 16 July 2025 report says Augsburg's Bauausschuss was due to decide on a new Stellplatzsatzung, required by Bavaria's rules from 1 October 2025 that set maximum rather than minimum parking figures. The proposal reduces required spaces for housing in the core and edge-core zones to 80 percent of the cap (down to 50 percent possible for climate adaptation) and raises the core-zone in-lieu fee from 13,500 to 18,000 euro; state rules cap new housing at 2 spaces per flat and bar parking obligations for single-family, semi-detached and row houses. The outcome of the vote is not stated.

items.note: PDF (73 pages, 'Die Mobilitätsstrategie des Augsburger Mobilitätsplans') p.15: public transport share 16-18 % since 2003; car use 41 % in 2018 at the same level as 2003; 'Ein Hinzugewinn von Marktanteilen für den ÖPNV ist jedoch nicht erkennbar'. Supported. Date: the document is marked 'Stand 2023' but file metadata is Sept 2024, and no page states adoption; the draft 'states' is fine. The conclusion 'little change in mode choice' is the author's gloss, partly valid (cycling share did rise). Corrected text drops that gloss.
items.corrected_text: The Mobilitätsstrategie of the Augsburger Mobilitätsplan states that the car share of trips was 41 percent in 2018, the same level as in 2003, and that public transport has held between 16 and 18 percent since 2003 with no visible gain in market share, while the cycling share of internal trips rose from about 14 percent in 2008 to over 19 percent in 2018.

items.note: Same PDF, pp.35 and 38: 'Szenario 2: Angebotsoffensive' is a modelled 'what if' scenario ('unterstellt'): tram/bus/cycling/walking expansion, measures for a car-light city centre (autoarme Innenstadt), spatial extension of Parkraumbewirtschaftung and higher fees, Tempo 30 across the network except a priority network. Correctly flagged as an assumption, not an adopted measure list. Same source as item 28 (could be merged).

corrected_summary: Augsburg charges 2.60 euro per hour for on-street parking in the Innenstadt zone and 1.00 euro elsewhere (ordinance of 28 March 2025), after the 2022 increase that abolished the free 30-minute Semmeltaste, and since April 2025 vehicles with an E-plate park free for up to three hours. Under the 2026 SPD-led coalition, CSU's Volker Ullrich floats bringing the Semmeltaste back, and the Radentscheid contract (to July 2026) included converting about 550 city-centre spaces; Mayor Florian Freund says the council will decide, so neither is settled. The Hauptbahnhof tram stop is expected to open between end of 2026 and mid-2027. The city lists 18 city-centre garages and a guidance system linking 15 of them, with real-time occupancy on its Smart City Dashboard; the Fuggerstraße garage was announced to close until September 2026 for cashless modernisation and now has 30 charging points, while demolition of the Kongress am Park garage was halted by a court injunction.
